key_insight: Long-range interactions let digital-analog quantum neural networks match short-range performance on supervised tasks with fewer layers or shorter evolution times.
engineering_relevance: Combining single-qubit gates with long-range analog entanglement can reduce circuit resources and classical optimization overhead, potentially easing implementation.
method: Alternate digital single-qubit operations with analog Ising evolution using power-law interactions.
Study how interaction range, transverse field, and evolution time affect expressibility and trainability.
Benchmark supervised image classification and many-body phase detection, plus unsupervised phase detection.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reduced layer or evolution-time requirements for supervised benchmarks and complementary long- and short-range signatures in unsupervised phase detection.
watch_item: Long-range ansatzes do not outperform short-range counterparts in every unsupervised regime, and the abstract provides no quantitative resource savings.
paper_title: Digital-Analog Quantum Neural Network with Long-Range Interactions
